title: 第1216章 租赁洞府第1215章 坊务堂
content_zh:
建筑的门面只有两间铺面的大小，门板敞开着，能看到里面的柜台和几张供人坐候的木椅。
这里就是金竹坊的管理处，负责坊市内洞府、院落、铺面的租赁和管理，以及日常的坊务协调和纠纷调解。
易长生跨过门槛走进了坊务堂的大厅。
大厅内部的空间比从外面看起来要宽敞一些，地面铺着普通的青砖，墙壁刷着白灰，墙角处放着一盆半枯的矮松盆栽。
正对着门口是一道长长的木制柜台。
柜台后面坐着一位穿着灰色长袍的中年修士，面容枯瘦，颧骨突出，眼窝略深，看起来大约四十多岁的模样。
修为在金丹初期，虽然不高的修为但作为坊务堂的管事足够用了。
他正低头手持一个玉简翻看着。
易长生走到柜台前面，站定，没有说话，只是安静地等着。
那位管事抬了一下眼皮，扫了他一眼，目光在他脸上停留了大约一息的时间，那是散修聚集地中每个人都会对陌生人做的那种快速评估和判断。
然后他重新低下头去，继续查看，口中随意地问道：“租洞府？还是租铺面？”
声音沙哑而平淡，带着一种每天要说上百遍同样话术的机械感。
“租洞府。”易长生的声音也相应地调整成了那种略微粗哑的低沉嗓音，语调平稳，带着一丝心幻平原散修特有的、不太爱多说话的冷淡。“长租的院子。”
管事从柜台下面的抽屉中取出一卷用细绳捆扎的兽皮纸，解开绳结后铺开在柜台上。
那兽皮纸上画着金竹坊的地形图，从山脚到山顶的各个区域都用不同颜色的线条和标记进行了划分。
他的手指在图纸上点了几下，从山脚下一片密集的小方格区域向上移动，经过一段标着淡蓝色的区域后停在了山腰偏下的位置。
“靠近山腰的院子，三进带后园和灵田。灵气浓度三阶上品，安静，安全，周围住的都是金丹后期的稳定住户，没什么闹事的。”
管事说话时手指在那一小片区域上画了个圈，“一年一千下品灵石。租不租？”
一千下品灵石。
这个价格在金竹坊中确实不算便宜，山脚那些只有一进小院、不带灵田的简陋住处大约只需要三四百灵石一年。

但山腰附近的院子确实有它的优势，灵气浓度更高、住户更稳定、纠纷更少，对于需要一个安稳落脚处的修士来说，多花的这些灵石物有所值。
易长生微微点了点头。
一千下品灵石对如今的他来说并不算什么大数目，他储物袋中的灵石储备虽然谈不上丰厚，但也足以支撑相当长时间的日常开销。
而且他目前的当务之急是找到一个安静、安全、不受打扰的地方安顿下来，而不是纠结于价格的高低。
他伸手从腰间取出一只普通的储物袋，从中数出十枚中品灵石放在柜台上。
content_en:
The facade of the building is only the size of two shops. The door panel is open, and you can see the counter inside and a few wooden chairs for people to sit and wait.
This is the management office of Jinzhufang, which is responsible for the leasing and management of caves, courtyards, and shops in the city, as well as daily coordination and dispute mediation.
Yi Changsheng crossed the threshold and walked into the hall of the Fangwu Hall.
The space inside the hall is wider than it looks from the outside. The floor is paved with ordinary blue bricks, the walls are painted with white dust, and a half-dry dwarf pine potted plant is placed in the corner.
Directly opposite the door is a long wooden counter.
Behind the counter sat a middle-aged monk wearing a gray robe. He had a thin face, prominent cheekbones, and slightly deep eye sockets. He looked about forty years old.
His cultivation level is at the early stage of Jindan. Although his cultivation level is not high, it is enough for him to be the steward of the Fang Wu Hall.
He was looking down at a jade slip in his hand.
Yi Changsheng walked to the counter, stood still, did not speak, and just waited quietly.
The steward raised his eyelids and glanced at him. His eyes stayed on his face for about a breath. It was the kind of quick assessment and judgment that everyone in a gathering of casual cultivators would make on strangers.
Then he lowered his head again, continued to check, and asked casually: "Rent a cave? Or rent a shop?"
His voice was hoarse and flat, with a mechanical feel as if he had to say the same words hundreds of times every day.
"Rent a cave." Yi Changsheng's voice was adjusted accordingly to a slightly rough and low voice, with a steady tone and a hint of indifference unique to Xinhuan Plains cultivators who didn't like to talk too much. "Long-term rental yard."
The steward took out a roll of animal skin paper tied with string from the drawer under the counter, untied the knot and spread it out on the counter.
The topographic map of Jinzhufang was drawn on the animal skin paper, and each area from the foot of the mountain to the top of the mountain was divided with lines and marks of different colors.
His fingers clicked on the drawing a few times, moving up from a dense small square area at the foot of the mountain, passing through a section marked with light blue, and stopped at a location lower down the mountainside.
"The courtyard close to the mountainside, with three entrances to the back garden and spiritual field. The aura concentration is at the third level and is of top grade. It is quiet and safe. The people around it are all stable residents in the late Jindan stage. There is nothing causing trouble."
The steward drew a circle on the small area with his finger as he spoke, "One thousand low-grade spiritual stones a year. Do you want to rent it?"
A thousand low-grade spiritual stones.
This price is indeed not cheap in Jinzhufang. The simple residences at the foot of the mountain that only have a small courtyard and no spiritual field only cost about three to four hundred spiritual stones a year.
But the courtyard near the mountainside does have its advantages. The spiritual energy concentration is higher, the residents are more stable, and there are fewer disputes. For monks who need a stable place to stay, the extra spiritual stones are worth the money.
Yi Changsheng nodded slightly.
A thousand low-grade spirit stones is not a big sum for him now. Although the reserve of spirit stones in his storage bag is not huge, it is enough to support daily expenses for a long time.
And his current top priority is to find a quiet, safe and undisturbed place to settle down, rather than obsessing over the price.
He reached out and took out an ordinary storage bag from his waist, counted out ten medium-grade spiritual stones and placed them on the counter.
